rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act rent cap
rules.requirement: Owners may not raise rent more than 5% plus the local CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, in any 12-month period, with at most two increases. Initial rent on a new tenancy is not capped.
rules.key_value: 5% + CPI, max 10%
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property generally, unless exempt.
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted/subsidized affordable housing; dormitories; housing under stricter local rent control; CO issued within previous 15 years; certain separately alienable properties (single-family homes, condos) with non-corporate owners and written notice; owner-occupied duplexes.
rules.interaction: Does not apply where local rent control restricts annual increases to less than the state cap.
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower

unverifiable_exemptions: single-family homes and condos owned by non-corporate, non-REIT owners with written notice

rules.penalty: Civil action for injunctive relief, damages, attorney's fees, up to 3x damages if willful; enforceable by AG, city attorney or county counsel.
rules.effective_date_note: Current version operative April 1, 2024 (effective Jan 1, 2024); the cap originally applied to increases on or after March 15, 2019.
rules.prior_version_note: AB 1482 cap in force since 2019-03-15 (rent increases on/after that date); SB 567 repealed and re-added it, operative 2024-04-01.

in_force_since_evidence.quoted_span: This section shall apply to all rent increases subject to subdivision (a) occurring on or after March 15, 2019

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act – Just Cause Eviction
rules.requirement: After a tenant has lived in a unit for 12 months, the landlord may end the tenancy only for a stated at-fault or no-fault just cause. For no-fault terminations the landlord must pay one month's rent in relocation assistance (within 15 days of notice) or waive the final month's rent.
rules.key_value: Just cause after 12 months; relocation = 1 month's rent for no-fault
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies of 12+ months (24 if additional adults added); does not apply where a local just cause ordinance applies.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels; certain care facilities; dormitories; shared kitchen/bath with owner; owner-occupied single-family and duplex; CO within previous 15 years; separately alienable non-corporate-owned property with notice; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing.
rules.interaction: Does not apply to property subject to a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before Sept 1, 2019 or a later more protective one.
rules.quoted_span: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy

unverifiable_exemptions: separately alienable property with non-corporate owner and exemption notice
dormitories, hospitals, care facilities, transient hotels

rules.penalty: Noncompliant notice void; actual damages, fees, up to 3x for willful violations; AG/city attorney may seek injunction.
rules.effective_date_note: Operative April 1, 2024 per subdivision (m); amended by AB 1529 effective 2026-01-01; repealed as of 2030-01-01.
rules.prior_version_note: AB 1482 just-cause rules applied from 2020 (notice dates July 1, 2020 in text); SB 567 made the section operative 2024-04-01 and AB 1529 amended it effective 2026-01-01.

rules.title: California security deposit cap and handling (AB 12)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not demand or receive more than one month's rent as security (two months for small natural-person landlords with no more than two properties and four units total; not for service members). Deposits must be returned with an itemized statement within 21 days of move-out.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords)
rules.coverage_conditions: Security for rental agreements of residential property used as the tenant's dwelling.
rules.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy

unverifiable_exemptions: landlord type and number of properties owned (two-month cap)
coverage.landlord_size_condition: Two-month cap only for natural person or all-natural-person LLC landlord owning no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four dwelling units total

rules.penalty: Bad-faith retention: statutory damages up to twice the deposit plus actual damages.

rules.title: California application screening fee cap and rules
rules.requirement: Screening fees may cover only actual out-of-pocket costs and time, capped at $30 per applicant adjusted annually for CPI (Berkeley Rent Board cites $68.96 for 2026). No fee if no unit is available; landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, and provide the credit report within 7 days.

rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords (owners of residential rental property) and their agents charging applicants.
rules.interaction: Applies notwithstanding Civ. Code § 1950.5; fee is not security.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant

rules.prior_version_note: The $30 per-applicant fee cap, CPI-adjustable since 1998-01-01, predates the AB 1170 amendment effective 2026-01-01; the CPI-adjusted dollar figure resets annually.

rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate against or harass applicants or tenants because of source of income, including Section 8 and other vouchers. rules.exemptions: Owner occupying a home and renting to one additional person; senior housing.

rules.title: AB 325 – Common pricing algorithm prohibition (Cartwright Act)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (used by two or more persons, using competitor data to set prices) as part of a conspiracy to restrain trade, or to use or distribute one while coercing others to adopt its recommended prices. Applies to all pricing including rents.
rules.key_value: ban on common pricing algorithms using competitor data in restraint of trade or with coercion
rules.coverage_conditions: Any person using or distributing a common pricing algorithm; not limited to housing; excludes end consumers.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter
rules.penalty: Cartwright Act violation; civil fines up to $1 million and increased criminal fines per D028.
rules.effective_date_note: Approved Oct 6, 2025; general effective date Jan 1, 2026 (D028 confirms).
rules.prior_version_note: Section 16729 was newly added to the Cartwright Act; before 2026 only general antitrust prohibitions applied.

rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act (good cause, notices, grounds)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not evict or fail to renew a residential lease without good cause listed in the Anti-Eviction Act. Except for nonpayment, a written Notice to Quit (often after a Notice to Cease) is required, with notice periods from 3 days to 3 years depending on the ground; self-help evictions are illegal. Owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings have separate rules (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2). Landlords who evict to occupy must occupy 6 months; removal from residential use carries a 5-year bar and penalties (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.6). Rent increases need a notice to quit and notice of increase.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.requirement: In housing funded by or on land from Boston DND, or with income-restricted units under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy, providers may not use blanket bans on applicants with arrests or convictions. They may not consider non-conviction arrests, expunged or sealed convictions, juvenile records, or convictions over 5 years old, with exceptions for direct relationship or unreasonable risk. Credit scores may not be used to approve or deny applications.
rules.key_value: No blanket criminal-history bans; no convictions older than 5 years; no credit score use
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land, or with income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply where a conviction has a direct relationship to the housing sought or poses unreasonable risk of substantial harm to others, or to current criminal behavior.
rules.interaction: Conflicting federal or state criminal-history requirements preempt this policy.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND, Feb. 2017)

rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance: tenant selection and source-of-income protection
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate in renting based on protected categories, including source of income (Section 8 and public benefits). Any tenant-selection standard must be reasonable and applied equally and uniformly to all applicants, such as ability to pay rent and to care for the apartment.
rules.key_value: No source-of-income discrimination (incl. Section 8); uniform reasonable standards
rules.exemptions: Exemption for 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there.
rules.quoted_span: Under the law, landlords, sellers and rental agents may use any reasonable standard to determine which applicants are selected, as long as that standard is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants
rules.penalty: Civil fines up to $300 per violation, plus injunctive relief, damages and other remedies after hearing.
rules.effective_date_note: Document gives no adoption date.
